sections.heading: Where this sits for you
body: **8 of the official questions in Boundaries are this one** — 0 Easy, 0 Medium, 8 Hard.
It is top-heavy: most versions are Hard, so it only earns study time once your target actually requires that tier.

sections.heading: How to spot it
body: You are looking at this pattern when:
- The blank sits between a descriptive title or role (a profession, sometimes with a field or nationality in front) and a person's name.
- The choices put commas before the name, after it, both, or neither, or use a colon or dash.

sections.heading: The method
body: - 1) Check for a 'the' or 'a' in front of the title.
- With no article, the title and name together act as one noun phrase, like a label.
- 2) Choose no punctuation between the title and the name, and no comma after the name before the verb.

sections.heading: What it is built to catch
body: You remember appositive commas ('my friend, Ana, said...') and apply them here.
Without an article, the name is essential to the meaning.
So a comma on either side, or a pair of them, is wrong.
A single comma after the name also splits the subject from its verb.

sections.heading: You are losing these
body: Before you choose, say out loud what the question is asking for — not what you solved for.
